# Enzyme release notes - v0.13.4

## Short version

Catalyst links are now scored when you search instead of being precomputed,
so indexes are about half the size and refresh after edits is roughly 10×
faster. Every note is embedded by default, stored vectors record which model
made them, and the embedding backend moves to encoders 3. A new
`enzyme compact` command returns the freed space to disk.

## What shipped

### Catalyst links on demand

- The precomputed catalyst-to-note similarity tables are gone. Search scores
  catalyst links from the stored vectors when it needs them: the catalyst shown
  beside each `catalyze` result, `--routing catalysts`, `--target` search, and
  the desktop explore views. (`4804ada`)
- `catalyze` returns the same notes in the same order. On a 4,700-note index
  the catalyst shown beside each result matched the old one 98.6% of the time;
  the rest differ because stored catalyst vectors are 8-bit.
- The same index drops from 389 MB to 174 MB once compacted, and a refresh
  after editing 25 notes goes from 2.6 s to 0.19 s. Searches take about
  10–25 ms longer, because each loads the stored vectors.
- `--target` folders now hold only their own notes and vectors, so preparing a
  target no longer depends on catalyst generation.

### Compacting the index

- `enzyme compact` rewrites the index file so freed space goes back to disk,
  and reports the size before and after (`--json` available). The old tables
  are dropped automatically on the first refresh after upgrading, but the file
  only shrinks when you compact it. (`bc717cd`)

### Embeddings

- Every note is embedded by default. The per-run cap (2,048 notes, adaptive up
  to 8,192) is gone, so a refresh catches up in one pass. An explicit
  `prepare up to N documents` / `max_embedding_files = N` still caps a run to
  the newest N. (`20b267b`)
- Stored vectors are tagged with the model, width, and quantization that made
  them, so a future model change re-embeds instead of mixing vectors. The
  first refresh after upgrading re-embeds every note once, locally, with no
  model calls; questions are kept. (`af3d7ad`)
- encoders 2 → 3: faster encoding, identical vectors for the model Enzyme uses.

## Behavior changes to check

- `refresh` JSON no longer has a `similarity` object or
  `similarities_recomputed`; it reports `catalysts_embedded` instead (normally
  0). The `similarities_incrementally_maintained` change reason is now
  `catalyst_vectors_embedded`.
- `ingest --quiet` reports `catalysts_embedded` instead of `similarity`.
- `init --json-progress` emits a `catalyst_vectors` stage instead of
  `similarity`.
- The desktop explore warm-up (`POST /explore/warm`) reports `chunks` instead
  of `similarities`.
- The first refresh after upgrading re-embeds the whole vault. That takes
  about a second for a few thousand notes.
